short: Sensor, murmur mode and HMM retraining (M05, M04, M03) are the authors' 2003 design, standard for lack of repetition; noise robustness lacks levels and an air baseline.
position: The paper [@nakajima2006nam] changes the sensor (M05), the speaking mode (M04) and the model transfer (M03); the design is the authors' own from their 2003 reports [@nakajima2003icassp; @nakajima2003eurospeech], and before 2004-03 no independent group had used a NAM microphone or recognized murmur. All three are standard because one speaker, tested speaker-dependently, gives no repetition. Rows A-C of Table 1 equal the 2003 table to rounding although the described training set is larger (§3.5). The noise-robustness claim lacks noise levels and a same-session air-microphone baseline; with noise played live at 60 dBA, a [later] same-group test fell from 83.7% to 53.3% (silicone microphone, one female speaker, 100 adaptation utterances) [@heracleous2007unvoiced]. The 93.3% in quiet is close to the best audited NAM dictation result, 93.9%, first reported in 2005 [@heracleous2005tissue].
